newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP reports lower interim steel output.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP reports lower interim steel output.

text.p: Resources and steel group The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd reported on Tuesday a drop in steel production for the first half to November 30, but posted stronger coal, iron ore, crude oil and condensate output.

The world's second biggest copper producer since buying Magma Copper in the United States in January, BHP also reported higher cathode output from its Escondida mine in Chile but lower output and shipments from Papua New Guinea for the six months.
BHP's copper concentrate production rose 41 percent to 352,400 tonnes for the first half, compared with the first six months of 1995/96, due to expansion of Escondida and the purchase of Magma.

BHP's struggling steel division reported a four percent drop in raw steel production for the first half of 1996/97, to 4.185 million tonnes, but despatches for the six months were six percent higher at 4.184 million tonnes.
"International (steel) market conditions are largely unchanged from the first half of calendar 1996," it said.

Coal output from Queensland state rose 15 percent in the first half to 11.772 million tonnes, iron ore 10 percent to 27.348 million tonnes, and oil and condensate three percent to 35.048 million barrels.
Gas output, including liquefied natural gas (LNG), fell four percent to 130.3 billion cubic feet.
